nodes.name: Case Triggered
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/vendor-onboarding/case with {case_id, action, metadata}. Responds 200 immediately: the assessment can take seconds, and a caller should not hold a connection open waiting for it. The outcome is written to the case audit trail, which is where the UI reads it from.

nodes.name: Workflow Settings
nodes.notes: Only place configuration is declared. The secret is read from the container environment by expression so it is never written into this workflow file.

nodes.name: Validate Trigger
nodes.notes: Rejects a malformed trigger before it can build a URL.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_TRIGGERED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({action: $json.action, trigger_metadata: $json.trigger_metadata}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Trigger Started
nodes.notes: Records WORKFLOW_TRIGGERED in the case audit trail.

nodes.name: Submit Case
nodes.notes: Moves the case from DRAFT into document collection. A 409 here is the idempotent path, not an error.

nodes.name: Interpret Submit
nodes.notes: Classifies the submit response; only a real failure stops the run.

nodes.name: Submission Ok?
nodes.notes: A case that cannot be submitted is not assessed.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_FAILED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({state: $json.submission_state, detail: $json.submission_detail, http_status: $json.submission_http_status}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Submission Blocked
nodes.notes: Terminal. The case never reached assessment.

nodes.name: Run Assessment
nodes.notes: The one call that does real work. It runs the deterministic rules, the explainable scorer, the document checks and the AI advisory inside the backend -- n8n only triggers it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'RETRY_EXHAUSTED', case_id: Number($('Validate Trigger').first().json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({stage: 'assessment', detail: 'Assessment call failed after 3 attempts.'}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Assessment Failure
nodes.notes: Terminal. Reached only after the retries are spent.

nodes.name: Interpret Assessment
nodes.notes: Maps the backend's route onto orchestration actions. Does not decide the route.

nodes.name: Get Eligible Reviewers
nodes.notes: Who may actually decide this approval type, according to the backend's authority table. The workflow does not keep its own copy of who is allowed to approve what.

nodes.name: Select Reviewer
nodes.notes: Deterministic pick, so a retry cannot route the same case to a different person.

nodes.name: Reviewer Available?
nodes.notes: With no eligible reviewer the case has nowhere to go, and that is escalated rather than ignored.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_FAILED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({stage: 'reviewer_resolution', reason: $json.reviewer_reason, route: $json.route}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record No Eligible Reviewer
nodes.notes: Terminal. An unstaffed queue is an operational failure, not a quiet no-op.

nodes.name: Notify Reviewer
nodes.notes: Best-effort. A notification failure is recorded but does not stop the approval from being opened -- the work is real even if nobody was told about it.

nodes.name: Interpret Notification
nodes.notes: Classifies the notification outcome; the approval opens regardless.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: ={{ $json.notification_state }}, case_id: Number($('Validate Trigger').first().json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({detail: $json.notification_detail, http_status: $json.notification_http_status, recipient: $json.recipient}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Notification
nodes.notes: Records SENT or FAILED; the approval still opens.

nodes.name: Route Decision
nodes.notes: One branch per route; no shared downstream node. Prevents double-execution on multi-branch fire.

nodes.name: Open Manager Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal. No findings; auto-approval path opened for manager.

nodes.name: Open Compliance Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal. Findings exist but none of them block completion.

nodes.name: Open Senior Compliance Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal. Routed to the compliance lead by the notification audience; the approval type itself is unchanged, because the authority table is the backend's to define.

nodes.name: Open Escalated Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal. Multiple or severe findings; senior review required.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_COMPLETED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({outcome: 'blocked_by_findings', route: $json.route, risk_score: $json.risk_score, detail: 'Blocking findings prevent completion. No approval opened; a reviewer must triage them first.'}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Blocked Case
nodes.notes: Terminal. A blocked case opens no approval on purpose: there is nothing to approve until the blocking findings are cleared, and opening one anyway would put a decision in front of a reviewer that they are not yet able to make.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_FAILED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({route: $json.route, detail: 'Route not recognised by this workflow version.'}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Unexpected Route
nodes.notes: Fallback output. Reached only if the backend returns a route this workflow does not know.

parameters.content:
## Vendor Onboarding — Case Orchestrator

Triggered by the backend when a case is ready to be assessed.

**This workflow contains no business logic.** It does not score, route, validate, or decide. It moves data in the right order, retries what can be retried, and records what it did.

The route comes back from the backend's deterministic rule engine and explainable scorer. The AI advisory is recorded beside it and never influences it.

### Idempotency

Re-running this workflow on the same case is safe. A case already past DRAFT answers 409 to the submit call, which is treated as success and the assessment continues.

Reviewer selection is deterministic, so a retry cannot deliver the same case to a different person.

### Branches

Each branch is a single terminal node. There is no shared node downstream of the switch: in n8n a node with several incoming branches executes once per branch that fires, which silently doubles audit writes when two branches light up. One terminal per branch makes that impossible.
